content: 1. Chronic hepatitis C has been treated with the antiretroviral drug abacavir. (Antiviral Therapy, 2008; 13(3):429–437). 2. Laufer N, Laguno M, Perez I, Cifuentes C, Murillas J, Vidal F, et al. conducted a study demonstrating that abacavir does not affect the virological response rate in patients co-infected with HIV and HCV who are treated with pegylated interferon and weight-adjusted ribavirin. (Antiviral Therapy, 2008; 13(7):953–957). 3. El-Raziky MS, El-Hawary M, Esmat G, Abouzied AM, El-Koofy N, Mohsen N, et al. investigated the prevalence and risk factors of asymptomatic hepatitis C virus infection in Egyptian children. (World Journal of Gastroenterology, 2007; 13(12):1828–1832). 4. Locasciulli A, Gornati G, Tagger A, Ribeiro ML, Cavalletto D, Cavalletto L, et al. explored hepatitis C virus infection and chronic liver disease in children with leukemia who are in long-term remission. (Blood, 1991; 78(6):1619–1622). 5. Rossetti F, Cesaro S, Pizzocchero P, Cadrobbi P, Guido M, Zanesco L. reported on chronic hepatitis B surface antigen-negative hepatitis following malignancy treatment. (Journal of Pediatrics, 1992; 121(1):39–43). 6. Jonas MM, Zilleruelo GE, LaRue SI, Abitbol C, Strauss J, Lu Y. studied hepatitis C infection in a pediatric dialysis population. (Pediatrics, 1992; 89(4 Pt 2):707–709). 7. Greco M, Cristiano K, Leozappa G, Rapicetta M, Rizzoni G. examined hepatitis C infection in children and adolescents undergoing hemodialysis and after renal transplantation. (Pediatric Nephrology, 1993; 7(4):424–427). 8. Nelson SP, Jonas MM. investigated hepatitis C infection in children who received extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. (Journal of Pediatric Surgery, 1996; 31(5):644–648). 9. Ni YH, Chang MH, Lue HC, Hsu HY, Wang MJ, Chen PJ, et al. studied post-transfusion hepatitis C virus infection in children. (Journal of Pediatrics, 1994; 124(5 Pt 1):709–713). 10. Thomas DL, Astemborski J, Rai RM, Anania FA, Schaeffer M, Galai N, et al. described the natural history of hepatitis C virus infection, focusing on host, viral, and environmental factors. (JAMA, 2000; 284(4):450–456). 11. Potthoff A, Wedemeyer H, Boecher WO, Berg T, Zeuzem S, Arnold J, et al. conducted the HEP-NET B/C co-infection trial, a prospective multicenter study investigating the efficacy of pegylated interferon-alpha 2b and ribavirin in patients co-infected with HBV and HCV. (Journal of Hepatology, 2008; 49(5):688–694). 12. Pérez-Elías MJ, García-San Miguel L, González García J, Montes Ramírez ML, Muriel A, Machín-Lázaro JM, et al. reported on tuberculosis complicating hepatitis C treatment in HIV-infected patients. (Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2009; 48(8):e82–e85). 13. Gilks CF, Crowley S, Ekpini R, Gove S, Perriens J, Souteyrand Y, et al. discussed the World Health Organization's public-health approach to antiretroviral treatment for HIV in resource-limited settings. (The Lancet, 2006; 368(9534):505–510).
